# Documentation history

Newest first.

## 2026-10-02 — first generation of the context tree

**Scope:** `docs/general-context/`, `docs/architecture/`, `docs/features/`, `00-INDEX.md`,
`FEATURE-MAP.md` · **Anchored to:** `c3@fcd0bd9` (`main`)
**How:** generated by `claude/opus` through sk-context (partition → architecture → features →
orientation), one agent per document, then gated.

First map of the codebase after v0.1.0: 11 product surfaces (3 at tier A — threads and requests,
sessions and agents, watcher and plugin; 6 at B; 2 at C) and 7 architecture axes. The hand-written
references `api.md`, `mcp.md` and `deploy.md` predate this tree and are not part of it.

**Known gaps:**
- 13 `_(undetermined)_` markers across 11 documents (admin UI, sessions and agents, join security,
  session lifecycle, event feed, configuration, build) — claims the agents could not settle from the
  code; open them before trusting those lines.
- Feature jobs were not told which files architecture owns, and several "Not owned here" tables
  pointed sweeper / idempotency / auth files at sibling features. Those rows were retargeted by hand
  to the architecture documents; the prose around them was not re-read.
- The `/watch` endpoint is split across two features: the action lives in the event-feed controller
  and the relevance rules in `C3.Watch` (watcher-and-plugin).
- Four files deliberately have no owner: `lib/c3.ex` (boilerplate) and the shared HTML shell
  (`core_components.ex`, `layouts.ex`, `layouts/root.html.heex`).
- Tiers come from the planned follow-ups, not from churn: the history is one commit per build phase.
- The routing check (closed tickets → files) was not run: there is only one, all-encompassing ticket.
